title: "what does my policy actually mean"
userSays: what does my policy actually mean

script.say: Your auto-approve limit is {{0.policy.outbound.humanClickAboveUsd}} dollars: above it you click. Your hard cap is {{0.policy.outbound.maxPerTransactionUsd}} dollars: above it nothing runs at all. They're both 100, so nothing ever waits for you: everything the cap allows runs on its own. Want me to lower the limit to 50?

rubric: The never-asks trap is stated as a consequence of these two numbers, not as a general warning.
mustSayText: the two numbers do different jobs: above the auto-approve limit they click, above the hard cap nothing runs at all. With both at $100 nothing ever waits for them, because everything allowed is also small enough to run on its own. It offers a fix, a lower limit or a higher cap; one question with a default is fine. Plain words, no table.
pass: zero propose_*; reply contains both "ask" and "cap" semantics and the sentence that nothing would ever wait for them.
